We examine e+e- --> Ds- Ds*+ and Ds*- Ds+ interactions at 4170 MeV using the CLEO-c detector in order to measure the decay constant fDs+. We use the Ds+ --> l+ nu channel, where the l+ designates either a mu+ or a tau+, when the tau+ --> pi+ nu. Analyzing both modes independently, we determine B(Ds+ --> mu+ nu) = (0.594 +- 0.066 +- 0.031)%, and B(Ds+ --> tau+ nu) = (8.0 +- 1.3 +- 0.4)%. We also analyze them simultaneously to find an effective value of B{eff}(Ds+ --> mu+ nu) = (0.638 +- 0.059 +- 0.033)% and extract fDs = (274 +- 13 +- 7) MeV. Combining with our previous determination of B(D+ -> mu+ nu), we also find the ratio fDs/fD+ = 1.23 +- 0.11 +- 0.04. We compare to current theoretical estimates. Finally, we find B(Ds+ --> e+ nu) < 1.3 x10^{-4} at 90% confidence level.

outputs.L1:
We study \(e^+e^- \to D_s^-D_s^{*+}\) and \(D_s^{*-}D_s^+\) interactions at a center-of-mass energy of 4170 MeV using the CLEO-c detector to measure the decay constant \(f_{D_s^+}\). We investigate the \(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu\) channel, where \(\ell^+\) denotes either a \(\mu^+\) or a \(\tau^+\), with \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+\nu\). Analyzing the two modes independently, we determine
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu)=(0.594\pm0.066\pm0.031)\%,
\]
and
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu)=(8.0\pm1.3\pm0.4)\%.
\]
A simultaneous analysis of both modes yields an effective branching fraction
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{eff}}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu)=(0.638\pm0.059\pm0.033)\%,
\]
from which we extract
\[
f_{D_s}=(274\pm13\pm7)\ \text{MeV}.
\]
Combining this result with our previous determination of \(\mathcal{B}(D^+ \to \mu^+\nu)\), we obtain
\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}}=1.23\pm0.11\pm0.04.
\]
We compare these results with current theoretical estimates. Finally, we establish the upper limit
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu)<1.3\times10^{-4}
\]
at the 90% confidence level.

The analysis considers \(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu\), with \(\ell^+\) representing either \(\mu^+\) or \(\tau^+\), and the \(\tau^+\) reconstructed through \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+\nu\).

Separate analyses of the two channels yield
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu)=(0.594\pm0.066\pm0.031)\%
\]
and
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu)=(8.0\pm1.3\pm0.4)\%.
\]

A combined treatment gives an effective branching fraction
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{eff}}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu)
=(0.638\pm0.059\pm0.033)\%,
\]
from which we obtain
\[
f_{D_s}=(274\pm13\pm7)\ \text{MeV}.
\]

When this result is combined with our earlier measurement of \(\mathcal{B}(D^+ \to \mu^+\nu)\), the decay-constant ratio is found to be

\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}}=1.23\pm0.11\pm0.04.
\]

These measurements are compared with contemporary theoretical predictions. We also set the 90% confidence-level upper limit
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu)<1.3\times10^{-4}.
\]
outputs.L3:
This study investigates electron–positron collisions producing \(D_s^-D_s^{*+}\) and \(D_s^{*-}D_s^+\) pairs at a center-of-mass energy of 4170 MeV. Using data collected with the CLEO-c detector, the analysis focuses on purely leptonic \(D_s^+\) decays to determine the decay constant \(f_{D_s^+}\), an important quantity for testing theoretical calculations of heavy-meson dynamics.

Independent analyses measure the branching fractions
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to\mu^+\nu)=(0.594\pm0.066\pm0.031)\%
\]
and
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu)=(8.0\pm1.3\pm0.4)\%,
\]
where the \(\tau^+\) is reconstructed through the decay \(\tau^+\to\pi^+\nu\). In each result, the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic.

A simultaneous analysis of the muon and tau channels yields an effective muonic branching fraction of
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{eff}}(D_s^+\to\mu^+\nu)
=(0.638\pm0.059\pm0.033)\%.
\]
From this measurement, the \(D_s^+\) decay constant is determined to be
\[
f_{D_s}=(274\pm13\pm7)\ \text{MeV}.
\]

When combined with an earlier measurement of \(D^+\to\mu^+\nu\), the result gives the ratio
\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}}=1.23\pm0.11\pm0.04.
\]
This ratio provides a useful test of theoretical predictions, including lattice-QCD calculations and other approaches to heavy-flavor meson dynamics.

The study also searches for the strongly helicity-suppressed decay \(D_s^+\to e^+\nu\). No significant signal is observed, leading to the upper limit
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to e^+\nu)<1.3\times10^{-4}
\]
at the 90% confidence level.
outputs.L4:
The decay constant \(f_{D_s}\) is determined from purely leptonic decays of the \(D_s^+\) meson using data collected with the CLEO-c detector at a center-of-mass energy of 4170 MeV. At this energy, the principal charm-strange production channels are \(e^+e^-\to D_s^-D_s^{*+}\) and \(e^+e^-\to D_s^{*-}D_s^+\). One \(D_s\) meson is fully reconstructed in a set of hadronic modes, thereby providing a tagged sample in which the leptonic decay of the accompanying \(D_s^+\) can be studied with low background. The photon from the \(D_s^*\to D_s\gamma\) transition is also included when forming the event kinematics.

Candidate \(D_s^+\to\mu^+\nu\) and \(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu\), with \(\tau^+\to\pi^+\nu\), decays are selected by requiring exactly one additional charged track opposite the reconstructed tag and little unmatched calorimeter energy. Because the final-state neutrinos are not detected, signal yields are extracted using the missing-mass-squared distribution. The muon channel produces a peak near zero, while the \(\tau\) channel has a broader distribution because it contains two neutrinos. Particle-identification and calorimeter information are used to distinguish muon-like and pion-like tracks and to suppress backgrounds from hadronic \(D_s\) decays and incorrectly reconstructed tags.

In the Standard Model, the leptonic decay rate is

\[
\Gamma(D_s^+\to \ell^+\nu)=
\frac{G_F^2}{8\pi}f_{D_s}^2|V_{cs}|^2
m_\ell^2m_{D_s}
\left(1-\frac{m_\ell^2}{m_{D_s}^2}\right)^2.
\]

The factor \(m_\ell^2\) reflects helicity suppression, making the electron mode extremely rare and the muon and tau modes experimentally more accessible. Using the measured branching fractions, together with the \(D_s\) lifetime, meson and lepton masses, and the CKM matrix element \(|V_{cs}|\), independent values of \(f_{D_s}\) are obtained from the muon and tau samples. The two channels are then combined, accounting for correlated systematic uncertainties.

The combined determination is

\[
f_{D_s}=274\pm13_{\rm stat}\pm7_{\rm syst}\ {\rm MeV}.
\]

When compared with the CLEO-c determination of the charged-\(D\) decay constant, the result gives

\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}}
=1.23\pm0.11_{\rm stat}\pm0.04_{\rm syst}.
\]

This ratio is particularly useful because several experimental and theoretical uncertainties cancel, allowing a sensitive test of lattice-QCD calculations and other predictions of flavor-symmetry breaking in heavy-light mesons. The agreement between the muon and tau measurements also tests the Standard Model expectation for lepton-flavor dependence in charged-current decays.

A search is additionally performed for the highly helicity-suppressed decay \(D_s^+\to e^+\nu\). No significant signal is observed, and the study sets the upper limit

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to e^+\nu)<1.3\times10^{-4}
\]

at 90% confidence level. Overall, the measurements provide a direct experimental determination of \(f_{D_s}\), a test of theoretical calculations of charm-meson decay constants, and a constraint on possible non-Standard-Model contributions to leptonic \(D_s\) decays.
outputs.L5:
### Analyzing CLEO Data in the MeV Range

CLEO was a particle-physics experiment designed to study collisions produced by the Cornell Electron Storage Ring. By analyzing data from the CLEO detector, researchers investigated the properties and decays of particles containing charm and bottom quarks, as well as the behavior of tau leptons.

Particle masses and decay energies are often expressed in megaelectronvolts, or **MeV**. One MeV equals one million electronvolts. Although the electronvolt is technically a unit of energy, particle masses are commonly reported in MeV/\(c^2\). For example, precise measurements may reveal differences of only a few MeV between related particle states.

Analyzing CLEO events involved reconstructing the trajectories and energies of particles produced in electron–positron collisions. Scientists combined detector signals to identify decay products and calculate invariant masses. Peaks in the resulting mass distributions indicated the presence of specific particles, while background events had to be modeled and removed statistically.

The accuracy of these measurements was crucial. An uncertainty of even a few MeV could affect comparisons with theoretical predictions. CLEO’s precise data therefore helped test the Standard Model, improve knowledge of quark interactions, and support the discovery and characterization of previously unobserved decay processes.

Using \(600~\mathrm{pb}^{-1}\) of \(e^+e^-\) collision data collected with the CLEO-c detector at a center-of-mass energy of \(4170\) MeV, we measure purely leptonic \(D_s^+\) decays in events with a fully reconstructed \(D_s^-\) tag. We obtain
\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to\mu^+\nu)=(0.565\pm0.045\pm0.017)\%,
\]
and, from \(\tau^+\to\pi^+\bar\nu\) and \(\tau^+\to e^+\nu\bar\nu\), respectively,
\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu)=(6.42\pm0.81\pm0.18)\%,
\]
and
\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu)=(5.30\pm0.47\pm0.22)\%.
\]
Their combination gives
\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu)=(5.62\pm0.41\pm0.16)\%.
\]
Using the Standard Model leptonic-decay expression, we determine
\[
f_{D_s}=(259.5\pm6.6\pm3.1)\ \mathrm{MeV},
\qquad
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}}=1.26\pm0.06\pm0.02,
\]
where the uncertainties are statistical and systematic. No evidence is found for \(D_s^+\to e^+\nu\), and we set the 90% confidence-level limit
\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to e^+\nu)<1.2\times10^{-4}.
\]
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

Using about \(600~\mathrm{pb}^{-1}\) of CLEO-c data collected near \(\sqrt{s}=4.17\) GeV, where \(D_s^\mp D_s^{*\pm}\) pairs are produced, the study fully reconstructed one \(D_s\) as a tag and searched for leptonic decays of the other through missing-energy and missing-mass distributions.

The principal results were

\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to \mu^+\nu_\mu)
   =(0.565\pm0.045_{\rm stat}\pm0.017_{\rm syst})\%,
\]

and, using \(\tau^+\to\pi^+\bar\nu_\tau\),

\[
\mathcal B(D_s^+\to \tau^+\nu_\tau)
   =(6.42\pm0.81_{\rm stat}\pm0.18_{\rm syst})\%.
\]

The measured ratio,

\[
\frac{\mathcal B(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu_\tau)}
     {\mathcal B(D_s^+\to\mu^+\nu_\mu)}
 =11.4\pm1.7_{\rm stat}\pm0.2_{\rm syst},
\]

was consistent with the Standard Model expectation of roughly \(9.8\), supporting lepton universality.

Combining the leptonic measurements and using the Standard Model decay-rate formula, CLEO-c extracted

\[
f_{D_s}=259.5\pm6.6_{\rm stat}\pm3.1_{\rm syst}\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Thus, the analysis provided precise absolute leptonic branching fractions and a percent-level determination of the \(D_s\) decay constant, broadly consistent with Standard Model expectations and contemporary theoretical calculations.

We report independent and simultaneous analyses of the purely leptonic decays \(D_s^+\to\mu^+\nu\) and \(D_s^+\to\tau^+\nu\), with \(\tau^+\to\pi^+\nu\). From the measured branching fractions and Standard Model expressions for the leptonic decay widths, we determine the decay constant to be
\[
f_{D_s}=(274\pm13_{\rm stat}\pm7_{\rm syst})~\text{MeV}.
\]
Combining this result with the corresponding determination of \(f_D\), we obtain
\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_D}=1.23\pm0.11_{\rm stat}\pm0.04_{\rm syst}.
\]
The two leptonic channels yield consistent results, and their relative rates are compatible with lepton-flavor universality. The measured ratio \(f_{D_s}/f_D\) agrees with theoretical expectations, while the central value of \(f_{D_s}\) lies above contemporary unquenched lattice-QCD predictions, with a discrepancy at the level of approximately two standard deviations.
